1800 GOT JUNK Pricing in Austin: 2026 Guide

If you’re scrolling through Austin’s fast‑growing neighborhoods and wondering how much it will cost to clear out that old couch, broken appliances, or a whole garage full of junk, you’ve landed in the right spot. In this guide we’ll break down everything you need to know about 1-800-GOT-JUNK? pricing for 2026, the factors that shape your bill, and tips to keep the cost low while still getting top‑notch service.

How 1-800-GOT-JUNK? Sets Its Prices

Transparent, Volume‑Based Pricing

Unlike many local haulers that charge by the hour or by the pound, 1-800-GOT-JUNK? uses a volume‑based model. The crew arrives with a set of standardized truck sizes, measures the space your junk occupies, and gives you a flat rate that covers loading, transport, and disposal.

Why Volume Matters More Than Weight

  • Efficiency: The team can load items quickly when they fit neatly into the truck’s cubic space.
  • Fairness: Heavy items like concrete blocks don’t inflate the price because the rate is based on volume, not weight.
  • Predictability: You know the exact amount you’ll pay before the truck rolls up.

Because of this model, the main driver of cost is how many “cubic feet” of junk you have. That’s why a quick, accurate quote is essential.

What Influences Your Final Bill?

Key Factors to Consider

  1. Amount of Junk: The more items you have, the more truck space you’ll need. A single 12‑ft. truck can hold roughly 6–8 cubic yards (≈ 160‑200 cubic feet).
  2. Type of Materials: Some items—like hazardous waste, tires, or electronics—require special handling and may incur a surcharge.
  3. Location & Accessibility: If the pickup spot is hard to reach (narrow streets, stairs, or limited parking), the crew may need extra time, which can add a small access fee.
  4. Seasonal Demand: Austin’s spring clean‑out rush or summer renovation boom can cause slight price variations.
  5. Promotions & Discounts: New‑customer coupons, military discounts, or recurring‑customer deals can shave off anywhere from $20 to $200.

What’s Not Included in the Base Rate?

While the base price covers loading, hauling, and disposal, certain services may be extra:

  • Removal of hazardous materials (asbestos, chemicals)
  • Disassembly of large furniture (e.g., taking apart a bed frame)
  • Extended labor beyond the standard 2‑hour window

Typical Price Ranges in Austin for 2026

Small Jobs (One‑Room Clean‑Out)

For a modest bedroom clean‑out—think a mattress, a few boxes, and a nightstand—expect rates between $149 and $199. This usually fits within a single 12‑ft. truck.

Medium Jobs (Two‑Room or Garage Clean‑Out)

Two rooms or a half‑filled garage (couch, TV, small appliances, yard waste) typically falls in the $225‑$350 bracket. You may need a larger truck or a second load if the volume exceeds 8 cubic yards.

Large Jobs (Full‑House or Whole‑Garage)

A comprehensive clean‑out—entire house, multiple appliances, construction debris—can range from $400 to $750. In some cases, especially with extensive renovation waste, the price can top $1,000.

Special Items & Surcharges

  • Electronics Recycling: $25‑$50 per item, depending on type.
  • Tires: $15 each.
  • Hazardous Waste: $75–$150 per load.

All prices above are based on 2026 market data for the Austin metro area and include any standard taxes.

How to Save Money on Your Austin Junk Removal

1. Prep Your Items Before the Crew Arrives

Group similar items together, break down large furniture, and keep everything on the ground. The less time the crew spends reorganizing, the more likely you’ll stay within the quoted volume.

2. Take Advantage of Seasonal Promotions

Keep an eye on the 1-800-GOT-JUNK? website and local newsletters for “Spring Clean‑Out” or “Holiday Disposal” discounts. Many customers save $30‑$75 simply by using a promo code.

3. Bundle Multiple Loads

If you have a lot of junk but can wait a week or two, ask about a multi‑load package. The company often offers a reduced per‑load rate for scheduled pickups.

4. Recycle On‑Your‑Own When Possible

Items like cardboard, paper, and clean wood can be taken to a local recycling center for free. This reduces the volume you need to pay for, especially if you’re close to a city recycling hub.
